items.q: Last-click attribution gives all the credit to the final click before a conversion.
items.why: Earlier ads that helped get there get no credit under this model.

items.q: Last-click attribution shows the whole customer journey.
items.why: It shows only the final click, so earlier steps are hidden.

items.q: A view-through conversion counts someone who saw an ad but did not click.
items.why: The conversion is credited if it happens within a set time after the view.

items.q: An impression is the same thing as a click.
items.why: An impression is an ad being shown. A click is a user choosing to interact.

items.q: Incrementality testing asks what would have happened without the ad.
items.why: It compares a group that saw the ads with a similar group that did not.

items.q: A third-party vendor can verify viewability and invalid traffic.
items.why: Independent measurement gives buyers and sellers a shared view.

items.q: A lookback window is how long after an ad a conversion can still be credited to it.
items.why: Longer windows credit more conversions, but can over-credit ads.

items.q: Click-through rate is the best measure of brand awareness.
items.why: Awareness is better measured with reach, recall or brand lift. Many people notice ads without clicking.
